events.title: Coalition Of The Willing Meets In Berlin And Urges A Winter Energy Truce
events.summary: Leaders and representatives of Ukraine's partners met in Berlin on 19 November for a Coalition of the Willing meeting attended by President Zelensky; US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner also came to the Chancellery for talks with Chancellor Friedrich Merz. In a joint statement, the leaders of Germany, France, the United Kingdom and Ukraine called on Russia to accept a winter energy ceasefire and a truce allowing safe passage for food exports in the Black Sea. Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said the meeting sent a clear message to Moscow to take peace talks seriously.

events.title: Coalition Agrees To Cut Electricity Tax And Cap Fuel Prices
events.summary: The leaders of the CDU/CSU and SPD agreed in the coalition committee on 18 November to cut the electricity tax for all consumers from January, after eight hours of talks. Funding is secured only for 2027, and a time-limited cap on fuel prices will also be introduced. The agreement drew criticism from within both coalition parties.

events.title: Constitutional Court Rejects BSW Bid For A Bundestag Election Recount
events.summary: The Federal Constitutional Court in Karlsruhe rejected on 18 November the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance's (BSW) complaint over the 2025 Bundestag election. The party had missed the five percent threshold by fewer than 10,000 votes and sought a recount. The court dismissed the complaint as inadmissible; Sahra Wagenknecht called it a wrong judgment.

events.title: Manuela Schwesig Re-elected Premier Of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern
events.summary: The state parliament in Schwerin re-elected Social Democrat Manuela Schwesig as minister-president of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern on 16 November, in the first round of voting, confirming her in office for a further five years. Schwesig has led the state since 2017 and now heads a coalition of the SPD, the Left and the Greens, after the SPD won 35.5 percent in the state election on 20 September.

events.title: Bundestag Passes Reform Giving Intelligence Services Wider Powers
events.summary: The Bundestag on 13 November passed a reform that gives Germany's intelligence services broader powers, including secretly entering homes and carrying out hacking operations; the foreign intelligence service BND gains operational powers such as disabling servers of state hacking groups abroad. The coalition presented it as a response to a sharper threat, and Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said intelligence agencies would become real secret services. The AfD and the Left criticised the expansion as excessive.

events.title: Drone Maker Quantum Systems Discloses Cyberattack
events.summary: The Bavarian drone manufacturer Quantum Systems, which supplies Ukraine, said on 12 November that it had been the target of a cyberattack in late October. The company said firms at the forefront of supporting Ukraine are being targeted precisely because their work matters to customers' security. A media report said the Bundeswehr had already responded. The company has not attributed the attack.

events.title: German Cabinet Approves Strategic Gas Reserve For Crises
events.summary: The German cabinet on 11 November approved plans for a new strategic gas reserve to prepare for sabotage or attacks on energy infrastructure. The reserve is to hold 24 terawatt-hours of additional physical gas, enough to secure supply for 30 days if deliveries fail completely, and is to be built up by Trading Hub Europe from 2027. It could be released only after the Federal Network Agency declares an emergency over a threatened gas shortage, and the government estimates the levy will cost households about four to seven euros a year.

events.title: Ilse Aigner Nominated As Union Candidate For Federal President
events.summary: The CDU's federal executive on 9 November backed Chancellor Friedrich Merz's proposal to nominate Ilse Aigner, the CSU president of the Bavarian state parliament, as the Union's candidate for federal president. The SPD leadership said it supports her. If elected by the Federal Convention, she would be Germany's first female head of state. On 10 November she presented herself to the Bundestag groups, but not to the AfD or the Left.

events.title: Bavarian Deputy Premier And Free Voters Leader Hubert Aiwanger Dies At 55
events.summary: Hubert Aiwanger, Bavaria's deputy minister-president and economy minister and the national leader of the Free Voters, was found dead in a Berlin hotel room on the evening of 4 November at the age of 55. Police and prosecutors opened an investigation into the cause of death, and investigators later said there was no indication of third-party involvement. Premier Markus Söder called his death an absolute tragedy, and a state memorial ceremony was held in Munich on 14 November.

events.title: Arrests In Raids On Alleged Communist Group In Saxony
events.summary: Saxony's state criminal police searched homes in Zwickau, Dresden, Leipzig, Saalfeld, Bremen and Hamburg on 3 November in a Dresden prosecutors' investigation into "Kollektiv Zwickau", which prosecutors allege formed in Zwickau in 2022 as a communist group to act against far-right structures. Twelve suspects aged 18 to 36 were under investigation, among other things on suspicion of forming a criminal organisation; four were arrested on warrants and a fifth was detained after allegedly attacking an officer. After eight more homes were searched on 11 November, the inquiry covers 20 suspects.

events.title: Hundreds Of Thousands Join Metal Industry Warning Strikes
events.summary: Workers in Germany's metal and electrical industries began warning strikes on 1 November, after the peace obligation in the IG Metall pay talks expired. The union said more than 413,000 employees had joined strikes and rallies by 6 November. IG Metall is seeking a 5 percent pay rise, while employers have offered 1.3 percent from July 2028.

events.title: Youth-Led Protests Turn To Rioting And Looting In German Cities
events.summary: Youth-led "Gen Z regelt" demonstrations for education, health and affordable living took place in cities across Germany on 31 October. The marches were largely peaceful during the day, but rioting broke out after dark in cities including Frankfurt, Cologne, Hamburg and Berlin. In Frankfurt, shops were looted and a gun shop was attacked; police said they seized two weapons there. Organisers distanced themselves from the violence.
